Class CreatedSlot

java.lang.Object
net.minecraft.world.inventory.Slot
com.trevlar.menukit.containers.api.slot.CreatedSlot
public class CreatedSlot extends net.minecraft.world.inventory.Slot
A slot that is a vanilla Slot to everything outside it. It keeps its place in the hierarchy (panel, group, index) in final fields and belongs to a SlotGroup.

It behaves like a vanilla slot. Every override calls super, so vanilla's behaviour and other mods' mixins still apply. It is also presented like one: its position is vanilla's own Slot.x/y, vanilla's slot pass draws it, and vanilla's getHoveredSlot finds it (see ContainerScreenLayers in MenuKit). A third party's extractSlot mixin, or any code that walks menu.slots and reads x/y, treats a created slot and a vanilla slot the same because they go through the same calls. The overrides:

  • mayPlace: false when inert, otherwise super
  • mayPickup: false when inert, otherwise super
  • getItem: EMPTY when inert, otherwise super
  • isActive: false when the panel is hidden, otherwise super

A mod that mixes into Slot.mayPlace to add a global filter sees its filter run on MenuKit slots through the super.mayPlace call, and the most restrictive answer wins. A mod iterating slots sees inert MenuKit slots as empty, which is a valid state for any slot.

Hierarchy: Screen, then Panel, then SlotGroup, then CreatedSlot.

    • isInert

      public boolean isInert()
      True when this slot's panel is hidden. To the outside world an inert slot looks like no slot at all: getItem returns EMPTY, mayPlace returns false, and shift-click skips it.

      Public for third parties that want to check directly rather than rely on those methods.

    • mayPlace

      public boolean mayPlace(net.minecraft.world.item.ItemStack stack)
      Whether this stack can be placed here. An inert slot refuses. Otherwise this is vanilla's own answer, which MenuKit's slot gate (MKSlotGateMixin) has already checked against this slot's address. Calls super, so a mixin on Slot.mayPlace still runs.

    • getItem

      public net.minecraft.world.item.ItemStack getItem()
      Returns the item in this slot, or ItemStack.EMPTY when the panel is inert, so a hidden panel's storage is never exposed.

      isActive(), mayPlace(ItemStack) and mayPickup(Player) returning false block interaction but not reading. Without this override, anything that reads slot.getItem() on a hidden slot (vanilla's broadcastChanges syncing to the client, other mods' mixins on Slot.getItem, consumer code walking menu.slots) would see the real contents. That would leak per-player state kept in hidden-panel storage (lock state, private inventories, sort state) to the client and to any mod hook.

      Returning EMPTY while inert prevents that. When the panel becomes visible, broadcastChanges sees the change and sends the real contents to the client. The backing Storage still holds the real items, and consumer code that owns the panel can read it directly.

      Inert means hidden from the world for both interaction and reading. Both are needed for the library's inertness guarantee (see the Inertness and SyncSafety probes in /mkverify all).

      Overrides:
      getItem in class net.minecraft.world.inventory.Slot

    • isActive

      public boolean isActive()
      Whether this slot is active (visible and usable).

      When false, vanilla skips the slot for rendering and hover detection. Together with getItem() returning EMPTY while inert, this hides the slot from the world entirely.
